chapter: Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and the bungalow
title: Drumming for the blues
summary: Blues needs slow tempo, a single bass drum beat and snare rolls; the roll is the essential skill of a drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, did you have any sort of special drumming accompaniment for a blues, Alec?
No, it's just a regular slow tempo, that's all.
Uh huh. Would you say that that is a fairly easy thing to play with the drums?
No, blues. There's nothing to play. A child can play the blues.
Well, when you say child play, what actually do you do?
I mean, just nothing but. Da da da. Da da da da da da da da da da da da da. That's all. And you make no roll or you make whatever you want. You know what I mean?
Well, you make one hit on the bass drum and then follow it with one.
Well, you got to make one beat for the blues.
One beat on the bass drum. Yeah.
You'll mess up a blues. You'll mess up a blues. You can't do too far in the blues. Or far in the blues.
Well I mean you get one on the bass drum and then follow with one on the snare drum.
Oh more than one on the stick. I mean you play your snare drum. They put you to work plenty of snare. You got plenty of snare work. On the blues?
Yeah. Oh yeah? Oh yeah. You be doing rolls and things?

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Sort of filling in? Oh yeah. And you got to make an even roll if you want to play it right. I mean something like that. I mean I'm not saying brag about myself but lots of people can't make a roll. No that's true. And they call themselves drummers. That's the most essential part of a drummer is a roll.
